newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE THE PLAYER TO BEAT AT LOCH LOMOND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE THE PLAYER TO BEAT AT LOCH LOMOND.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie's brilliant final round 62 to clinch the Irish Open on Sunday has left him red-hot favourite for the Loch Lomond World Invitational which begins on Wednesday.

The Invitational, which has attracted big names like Greg Norman and U.S. Open winner Ernie Els, is the last tune-up for next weeks's British Open at Royal Troon -- where Montgomerie's father is the secretary -- and provides the Scot with a chance to wipe out the memories of a year ago.

On that occasion, a seven-day period over the same two weeks left Montgomerie with a bad taste in his mouth. His closing 81 at windswept Carnoustie in the Scottish Open was followed by missing the cut at the British Open at Royal Lytham for the fourth time in five years.
He went on to missed the cut three weeks later at the U.S. PGA.
But at the end of the season, after he has won the European Order of Merit for the fourth successive year, he was philosophical about that lean period.
"I tend to leave my worst rounds of the year to the third week in July," he said.
"But my slump lasted just a few weeks. Most people's last longer. Then I started winning again."

He also won the Irish Open last year just ahead of his slump, but his form this year which brought recent wins in the European zone of the Andersen Consulting world championship and the European Grand Prix as well as second place to Els in the U.S. Open, is compelling.
The players strung out behind him at Druid's Glen on Sunday included the fast-rising Lee Westwood, Nick Faldo, Ian Woosnam and Jose Maria Olazabal.
"I took great heart from winning so well against such a strong field," Montgomerie said.
His rivals were left in no doubt about the state of Montgomerie's game.
"He stormed the golf course. I don't think I'll see a better round than that," Olazabal said on Monday.

The field builds up this week as the countdown continues for next week's British Open with British Open champion Tom Lehman and 1996 U.S. Open champion Steve Jones joining Els and Norman as the pick of the foreign players vying for the 133,330 pounds ($225,000) winner's cheque.
Els is making his first appearance since completing his U.S. Open and Buick Classic double last month.
"I've had two weeks off and I'm a bit rusty," he said. "But the course is magnificent. The par threes are great, very tough."
Norman, who played Loch Lomond for the first time at the weekend, agreed. "I was very impressed by the conditioning of the course. It is superb."
The beautiful layout beside the famous Scottish lake staged the event for the first time late last year when the winner was Dane Thomas Bjorn.
This year, with the demise of the Scottish Open, it has shifted into the pre-British Open week and attracted a much stronger field.
